value: 54,500 USD/TEU central; 27,250 and 109,000 as low/high sensitivity settings
basis_and_scope: Central value is the 2020 global average reported by Notteboom, Pallis and Rodrigue (S08), derived from UNCTAD shares and containerized TEU; it is not lane-, product- or year-specific. Low/high are sensitivity settings, not observations. V enters f_E, c_div_E, c_div_G and c_st_G jointly.

assumption: FEU to TEU quantity conversion for the WCI
basis_and_scope: Applied to quantity only. Spot rates are not linear in box size (Maersk, for example, prices some surcharges at 2x and some at less than 2x per 40ft).

assumption: Box type for the Hormuz Emergency Freight rate
value: 20' dry figure (1,800 USD) taken as the per-TEU charge
basis_and_scope: The 40' dry figure implies 1,500 USD per TEU; the 20' figure is the higher of the two per TEU.

value: Assessments dated 1 Jan-30 Nov 2023 that are available (20 values)
basis_and_scope: The calibration uses this assessment window. 2022 is excluded because rates were still falling from the pandemic peak. Missing weeks are not interpolated. The WCI is a spot index; contract rates paid by shippers can differ.

assumption: Diversion surcharge mapped to the Cape detour only
value: TDS applies to cargo subject to diversion; Maersk's PSS applies to all cargo regardless of routing and is not included
basis_and_scope: The model has no market-wide crisis freight term, so the PSS (500 USD per 20DRY from 1 Jan 2024 on FEA to North Europe) is not represented. One carrier's notice is used as representative of published charges.

assumption: Hormuz Emergency Freight rate applied to the diverted share
value: In the model the charge is paid on cargo that cannot pass Hormuz
basis_and_scope: Maersk applies the rate to all cargo to and from the listed Gulf countries from 2 March 2026; during the closure almost all ocean cargo is diverted in the model, but the charge also applies to partial diversion before the war (Nov 2025-Feb 2026), when no such surcharge existed.

assumption: Storage tariff mapped to the outside-port queue
value: 25 USD per TEU-day after 14 free days, i.e. 175 USD per TEU-week after two weeks
basis_and_scope: Maersk's storage-in-transit tariff for Option A; terminal tariffs for cargo cleared as import differ and are not used. Inventory holding cost h is charged separately on on-hand stock only, so there is no double counting.
